evidence.section: 3.1. Effect of Nb and Mo elements on the microstructure of the alloys
evidence.quote: While Nb and Ti atoms will diffuse into the β-phase, resulting in the β-phase being Al-lean, Nb-rich and Ti-rich to produce β-segregation. The dotted brighter phase at the boundary of the lamellae colonies is the production of β-segregation.

evidence.section: 3.1. Effect of Nb and Mo elements on the microstructure of the alloys
evidence.quote: When the TiAl alloys contain high Al content (> 44 at.%) and low β-phase stable element content, S-segregation occurs during the transition from the L-phase to the β-phase.

evidence.section: 3.1. Effect of Nb and Mo elements on the microstructure of the alloys
evidence.quote: If there are excess β-phase stable elements in α phase, the α-phase will transform into α2 + γ + β phases, which is called α-segregation in TiAl alloys.

evidence.section: 3.2. Effect of Nb and Mo elements on the mechanical properties of the alloys

evidence.section: 3.3. Effect of Nb and Mo elements on the oxidation resistance of the alloys
evidence.quote: (1) when ions with valence + 5 or + 6, such as Nb, are incorporated in the scale, oxygen vacancy concentration decreases and the growth of TiO2 may be suppressed [12].

evidence.section: 3.3. Effect of Nb and Mo elements on the oxidation resistance of the alloys
evidence.quote: (2) the activity of Al can be increased and promotes the diffusion of Al, which is very advantageous to form a continuous Al2O3 oxide film [18].

evidence.section: 3.3. Effect of Nb and Mo elements on the oxidation resistance of the alloys
evidence.quote: Mo can reduce the concentration of O in the matrix, impede the diffusion of Ti, and promote the diffusion of Al to induce the generation of continuous Al2O3 oxide film, resulting in the improvement of oxidation resistance [19,23].
